title: GS21 with the priced y factor on production, exposure = standardized PRODUCTIVITY (gvyz10), and an EXOGENOUS capital structure: three leverage types with the coupon per unit capital fixed at 0.15, 0.40, 0.70, drawn independently of productivity
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when the exposure is a PRODUCT of a hidden type and a within-firm state, so the premium is an interaction the ranks cannot span?
notes: 2026-10-21. gvyz10 (exposure 0.10 z~ y, no coupon term) plus a fixed coupon per type: the firm refinances to b_f whenever it can and never chooses otherwise (gs_blo = gs_bhi = b_f in gs_solve_vy.py). Equity's exposure to y is then productivity x the leverage multiplier with the multiplier independent of z: the structural version of gvyp10's product, with no term in the production function. In gvyz10 the endogenous coupon per unit capital runs 0.17-0.46 (p10-p90), rank-correlates -0.9 with size and 0.0 with roe, and the true premium's slope in leverage flips sign across roe quintiles (-0.20% to +0.22% a month per sd of leverage) but adds only 2 points of R2 over the additive fit: the product exists and leverage is not dispersed enough to matter. 0.70 puts the high-leverage type near distress (after-tax cash flow 0.8 (prod - delta - 0.70) with prod ~ e^{x+z} around 1).

changes: gs_bv [0.1, 0.1, 0.1] x (gs_bzl 0.0 + gs_bzi 1.0 z~): type x productivity exposure, bv_comp 0.0
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

method.gs_vy_exposure: production x exp(gs_bv (gs_bzl + gs_bzi z~) y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
